levels.title: Oral Language & Phonological Foundation
levels.description: Listen, speak, and play with sounds in words. Grade R–1, voice only, entry level. All 8 skills must be shown correctly at least 3 times each, across 2 different sessions at least 24 hours apart, with no help or hints.

atomic_skills.title: Multi-Step Instruction Following
atomic_skills.description: Follow spoken instructions with 2–3 steps, in the right order. The learner hears the instruction once and carries out each step correctly — no repeating, no hints.

error_signatures.description: A step was skipped entirely
error_signatures.example: Learner completes steps 1 and 3 but omits step 2

error_signatures.description: Steps completed but done out of order
error_signatures.example: Learner does step 3 before step 1

error_signatures.description: Learner needed the instruction repeated before responding
error_signatures.example: Learner asks 'Can you say that again?' before attempting

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: OMISSION: rebuild from 1-step instructions. SEQUENCE_ERROR: add visual order cues. PROMPT_DEPENDENCE: shorten instruction length.

atomic_skills.title: Story Retell with Sequenced Events
atomic_skills.description: Retell a story they heard, with at least 3 events in the correct sequence. The learner uses their own words to describe what happened, in order.

error_signatures.description: Fewer than 3 events recalled in the retell
error_signatures.example: Learner only mentions one thing that happened in the story

error_signatures.description: Events recalled but placed out of order
error_signatures.example: Learner describes the ending before the beginning

error_signatures.description: Learner cannot recall events from the source story without prompting
error_signatures.example: Learner says 'I don't remember' or gives unrelated content

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: LOW_EVENT_COUNT: scaffold with 'What happened next?' prompts. SEQUENCE_INVERSION: model using physical props. COPY_FAIL: model using physical props.

atomic_skills.title: Grammatically Complete Spoken Sentences
atomic_skills.description: Speak in full sentences — not just single words or fragments. Every response should have a subject and a verb, without needing prompting.

error_signatures.description: Response is missing a subject or verb
error_signatures.example: Learner says 'Running fast' instead of 'The dog is running fast'

error_signatures.description: Only a single word produced as the full response
error_signatures.example: Learner says 'Dog' when asked to describe the picture

error_signatures.description: Learner repeats the prompt verbatim instead of constructing a response
error_signatures.example: Prompt: 'What did you do today?' Response: 'What did you do today?'

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: FRAGMENT: provide sentence frame scaffolds. ONE_WORD: expand and recast. ECHO: switch to open-ended questions only.

atomic_skills.title: Rhyme Generation and Identification
atomic_skills.description: Identify words that rhyme, and make up their own rhyming words. The learner hears a word and says a word that sounds the same at the end — and can tell when two words rhyme or don't.

error_signatures.description: A non-rhyming word is produced in response to a rhyme prompt
error_signatures.example: Given 'cat', learner says 'dog' instead of 'hat'

error_signatures.description: Learner gives a word linked by meaning rather than sound
error_signatures.example: Given 'cat', learner says 'kitten' (related meaning, not rhyme)

error_signatures.description: Learner incorrectly identifies a non-rhyming pair as a rhyme
error_signatures.example: Learner says 'cat' and 'can' rhyme

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: NON_RHYME_GEN: run rhyme discrimination drills first. ASSOCIATION_ERROR: explicitly teach 'sounds like, not means like'.

atomic_skills.title: Syllable Segmentation and Blending
atomic_skills.description: Clap out the syllables in a spoken word, and blend syllables back together. The learner taps once for each part of a word, and can merge syllable chunks back into the whole word.

error_signatures.description: Too many taps — more syllables counted than exist
error_signatures.example: Learner taps 3 times for 'rain-bow' (2 syllables)

error_signatures.description: Two syllables collapsed into one tap
error_signatures.example: Learner taps once for 'cup-board' (2 syllables)

error_signatures.description: Learner cannot merge the syllable segments back into the full word
error_signatures.example: Given 'rain' + 'bow', learner cannot produce 'rainbow'

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: OVER_SEG: model with learner's own name. UNDER_SEG: exaggerate each syllable. BLEND_FAIL: reduce to 2-syllable words.

atomic_skills.title: Phoneme Isolation — Onset and Coda
atomic_skills.description: Pick out the first and last sound in a word. The learner hears a spoken word and says the very first sound, then the very last sound — with no letters or print involved.

error_signatures.description: Wrong first sound identified
error_signatures.example: For 'sun', learner says /z/ instead of /s/

error_signatures.description: Wrong last sound identified
error_signatures.example: For 'cat', learner says /k/ instead of /t/

error_signatures.description: Learner says the letter name instead of the phoneme sound
error_signatures.example: For 'bat', learner says 'bee' instead of /b/

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: ONSET_ERROR: drill with alliterative word sets. CODA_ERROR: use CVC words with a clapped final tap. NAME_SUB: explicitly teach 'the sound, not the name'.

atomic_skills.title: Full Phoneme Segmentation and Blending
atomic_skills.description: Break a word into its individual sounds, and blend sounds back into a word. The learner says each separate sound in a spoken word one by one, and can put a list of sounds back together into the right word.

error_signatures.description: A phoneme is missing from the segmented output
error_signatures.example: For 'cat', learner says /k/ /t/ omitting the vowel /a/

error_signatures.description: An extra phoneme inserted into the segmented output
error_signatures.example: For 'cat', learner says /k/ /a/ /t/ /s/

error_signatures.description: Phonemes produced in wrong order
error_signatures.example: For 'cat', learner says /t/ /a/ /k/

error_signatures.description: Blended output doesn't match the target word
error_signatures.example: Given /k/ /a/ /t/, learner produces 'cut' instead of 'cat'

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: PHONEME_OMIT: Elkonin box drill (a box for each sound). SEQ_ERROR: use a left-to-right physical counter. BLEND_FAIL: reduce to 2-phoneme sequences.

atomic_skills.title: Phoneme Manipulation — Deletion and Substitution
atomic_skills.description: Swap or remove a sound in a word to make a new word. For example: say 'bat' without the /b/, or change the /b/ in 'bat' to /s/ to make 'sat'. The learner manipulates sounds in their head — no print involved.

error_signatures.description: Incorrect phoneme was deleted from the word
error_signatures.example: Asked to say 'bat' without /b/, learner says 'ba' removing the final /t/

error_signatures.description: Wrong phoneme was swapped in during substitution task
error_signatures.example: Asked to change /b/ in 'bat' to /s/, learner produces 'tab'

error_signatures.description: Response took longer than 5 seconds
error_signatures.example: Learner pauses more than 5 seconds before responding

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: WRONG_PHONEME_REMOVED: segment the word before deleting. HIGH_LATENCY: reduce to onset deletion only and rebuild automaticity.

levels.title: Alphabetic Code Construction
levels.description: Learn the sound each letter makes, quickly and automatically. Grade 1, voice + text. Unlocks after Level 1. At least 95% accuracy with mean response time of 2.5 seconds or less, confirmed across 2 separate sessions. Speed matters as much as accuracy — average response time over 4 seconds sends the learner back to Level 1 drills.

atomic_skills.title: Letter-to-Sound Retrieval (Flashcard)
atomic_skills.description: Say the sound (not the name) of every letter — uppercase and lowercase — within 2.5 seconds. When shown a letter, the learner says the phoneme it makes, not what it's called.

error_signatures.description: Learner says the letter name instead of the phoneme sound
error_signatures.example: Sees 'b', says 'bee' instead of /b/

error_signatures.description: Incorrect sound produced for the letter shown
error_signatures.example: Sees 's', produces /z/ sound

error_signatures.description: Response time exceeds 2.5 seconds
error_signatures.example: Learner pauses 3 seconds before producing the sound

error_signatures.description: Learner confuses visually similar letters such as b/d, p/q, or m/w
error_signatures.example: Sees 'b', produces /d/ sound

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: NAME_HABIT: run 'sound only' drill mode. HIGH_LATENCY: timed flashcard mode. VISUAL_CONF: dedicated anchor drill before returning to full set.

atomic_skills.title: Bidirectional Letter-Sound Mapping
atomic_skills.description: Connect letters to sounds in both directions: letter → sound, and sound → letter. The learner can go from a letter to its sound AND pick the right letter when they hear a sound.

error_signatures.description: Passes forward (letter to sound) but fails backward (sound to letter)
error_signatures.example: Can say /b/ for 'b' but cannot select 'b' when hearing /b/

error_signatures.description: Two different letters mapped to the same phoneme
error_signatures.example: Both 'b' and 'd' mapped to the same /b/ sound

error_signatures.description: No discernible letter-to-sound mapping — responses appear random
error_signatures.example: Learner selects random letters when hearing phonemes

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: UNIDIRECTIONAL_ONLY: backward mapping drills. CONFLATION: isolate the confused pair and drill the contrast. RANDOM: regress to L1.

atomic_skills.title: Visually Confusable Letter Discrimination (b/d, p/q, m/w)
atomic_skills.description: Correctly tell apart look-alike letters: b/d, p/q, and m/w. The learner can look at each letter and say exactly which one it is — no mix-ups allowed.

error_signatures.description: b and d swapped
error_signatures.example: Learner reads 'b' as 'd' or vice versa

error_signatures.description: p and q swapped
error_signatures.example: Learner reads 'p' as 'q' or vice versa

error_signatures.description: m and w swapped
error_signatures.example: Learner reads 'm' as 'w' or vice versa

error_signatures.description: Correct in some orientations but not others
error_signatures.example: Correctly identifies 'b' in isolation but not in flashcard context

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: Any pair failure: specific anchor drill for that pair. Do not advance Tier 1 until zero errors on all three pairs.

atomic_skills.title: Digraph Phoneme Retrieval
atomic_skills.description: Produce the correct single sound for digraphs like sh, ch, th, wh, ck, and ng. Two letters make one sound — the learner says that one sound, not two separate letter sounds.

error_signatures.description: Learner produces two separate letter sounds instead of one digraph phoneme
error_signatures.example: For 'sh', learner says /s/ then /h/ separately instead of /sh/

error_signatures.description: Incorrect phoneme produced for the digraph
error_signatures.example: For 'ch', learner says /k/ instead of /ch/

error_signatures.description: Response time exceeds 2.5 seconds
error_signatures.example: Learner takes 3 seconds to retrieve digraph sound

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: COMPONENT_PHONEMES: model the digraph as a single unit. WRONG_SOUND: return to individual letter sounds. SLOW: timed drill mode.

atomic_skills.title: Consonant Blend Production
atomic_skills.description: Say both sounds in a consonant blend (e.g. 'st', 'bl') in the right order. The learner sees a blend and says each of its two sounds correctly, one after the other — no vowel sneaking in between.

error_signatures.description: Second phoneme of the blend produced before the first
error_signatures.example: For 'st', learner produces /t/ /s/ instead of /s/ /t/

error_signatures.description: Only one phoneme of the blend produced
error_signatures.example: For 'st', learner only says /s/

error_signatures.description: A vowel sound inserted between the consonants of the blend
error_signatures.example: For 'st', learner says /s/ /uh/ /t/

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: ORDER_REVERSAL: left-to-right physical cue. INTRUSIVE_VOWEL: exaggerate the blend inside a word with no pause; model until eliminated.

atomic_skills.title: Vowel Team Phoneme Retrieval
atomic_skills.description: Say the correct sound for vowel teams like ai, ee, oa, and oo — as one sound, not two. The learner sees a vowel team and produces a single fused phoneme, not two separate vowel sounds.

error_signatures.description: Learner produces two individual vowel sounds instead of the team phoneme
error_signatures.example: For 'ai', learner says /a/ then /i/ instead of the long /a/ sound

error_signatures.description: Long vowel of the wrong letter produced
error_signatures.example: For 'oa', learner produces the long /a/ sound instead of long /o/

error_signatures.description: Response time exceeds 2.5 seconds
error_signatures.example: Learner pauses more than 2.5 seconds before responding

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: SPLIT_VOWEL: present vowel team inside a known word first (e.g., 'rain' contains 'ai'). WRONG_LONG_VOWEL: contrast drill between the confused teams.

atomic_skills.title: Randomised 40-Item Phonogram Retrieval
atomic_skills.description: Retrieve the correct sound for any letter, digraph, blend, or vowel team from a mixed 40-item set in under 2.5 seconds. Tests whether sound knowledge is fully automatic across all phonogram types — not just one category at a time.

error_signatures.description: Any single item exceeds 4.0 seconds latency
error_signatures.example: Learner takes 5 seconds to retrieve the sound for 'ng'

error_signatures.description: Total accuracy falls below 95%
error_signatures.example: Learner gets 3 or more items wrong in a 40-item set

error_signatures.description: Multiple failures within the same phonogram type (e.g., all digraph errors)
error_signatures.example: Learner fails 'sh', 'ch', and 'th' but passes all single letters

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: LATENCY_OUTLIER: target failed items in isolation. CLUSTER_FAIL: drill that phonogram cluster type; return to full set only after cluster passes.

atomic_skills.title: Phoneme Sequence Blending into Words
atomic_skills.description: Blend a sequence of individual sounds spoken one at a time into the full word. The learner hears each sound in isolation and combines them smoothly to produce the complete word — the opposite direction to encoding.

error_signatures.description: Only 1-2 phonemes produced instead of the full blended word
error_signatures.example: Given /k/ /ae/ /t/, learner only says /k/ /ae/

error_signatures.description: Correct phonemes blended but in wrong order
error_signatures.example: Given /k/ /ae/ /t/, learner produces 'tack'

error_signatures.description: Output phonemically unrelated to the target word
error_signatures.example: Given /k/ /ae/ /t/, learner produces 'big'

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: PARTIAL_BLEND: reduce to 2-phoneme blends. TARGET_MISS: return to L1.C2 blending task.

levels.title: Encoding Consolidation — HARD GATE 1
levels.description: Spell words by matching sounds to letters. Grade 2, mainly text input. HARD GATE 1: Level 4 is completely locked until this level is passed — no exceptions, no overrides. At least 80% of encoded words must be plausible (every sound has a letter, in the right order), including made-up words, confirmed across 3 separate sessions.

atomic_skills.title: CVC Word Encoding — Real and Nonsense
atomic_skills.description: Type a plausible spelling for short CVC words (including made-up ones like 'zolp') — one letter per sound. The learner hears a word and types each sound as a letter, in the correct order, without help.

error_signatures.description: Vowel phoneme has no grapheme in the typed output
error_signatures.example: For 'cat', learner types 'ct'

error_signatures.description: Any phoneme is left unrepresented in the typed output
error_signatures.example: For 'sun', learner types 'sn'

error_signatures.description: Output shares only 1 or fewer phonemes with the target — suggests visual guessing
error_signatures.example: For 'blof', learner types 'blow' — a real word with no phonetic match

error_signatures.description: Phonemes encoded but in wrong left-to-right order
error_signatures.example: For 'cat', learner types 'tac'

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: VOWEL_OMIT: Elkonin box drill with explicit vowel slot. VISUAL_GUESS: nonsense-only words. SEQ_ERROR: left-to-right tap before writing.

atomic_skills.title: Blend and Complex Pattern Encoding (CCVC, CVCC)
atomic_skills.description: Type plausible spellings for longer words with blends and digraphs (e.g. 'stomp', 'chin'). The learner must capture every sound in the word — including blends — in the right order, without dropping letters.

error_signatures.description: One phoneme of a blend omitted in the encoding
error_signatures.example: For 'stop', learner types 'sop' omitting the /t/

error_signatures.description: Blend phonemes encoded in wrong order
error_signatures.example: For 'stop', learner types 'tsop'

error_signatures.description: A digraph encoded as two separate letters rather than as a unit
error_signatures.example: For 'ship', learner types 'shipp' treating sh as two sounds

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: BLEND_PARTIAL: isolate blend in speech, tap each phoneme, then encode one at a time. DIGRAPH_SPLIT: model digraph as a single unit.

atomic_skills.title: Unfamiliar Real Word Encoding via Phonological Analysis
atomic_skills.description: Encode unfamiliar real words using sound logic — not from memory. The learner must break each new word into sounds and find a letter for each one, proving they are using the phonics code rather than remembering what words look like.

error_signatures.description: Output matches a common word without phonetic logic — suggests visual memorisation
error_signatures.example: For an unfamiliar word, learner writes a known high-frequency word that doesn't match phonetically

error_signatures.description: Inconsistent phoneme-grapheme mapping for the same phoneme across different words
error_signatures.example: The /sh/ sound spelled 'sh' in one word but 's' in another with no pattern

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: MEMORISATION_FLAG: switch to nonsense words immediately. PHONEME_GUESSING: return to L2 phonogram drill for the failing phoneme type.

atomic_skills.title: Nonsense Word Encoding — Code Proof
atomic_skills.description: Encode made-up words with plausible phoneme-to-letter matches — this is mandatory for passing Hard Gate 1. Because the word doesn't exist in memory, the only way to spell it correctly is to use the phonics code. This skill proves the learner is a coder, not a memoriser.

error_signatures.description: Learner writes a real word instead of encoding the nonsense word — automatic fail
error_signatures.example: For 'blof', learner writes 'blow'

error_signatures.description: A phoneme from the nonsense word is missing in the encoding
error_signatures.example: For 'spund', learner writes 'spud' omitting /n/

error_signatures.description: A grapheme used that has no phoneme correspondence to the target
error_signatures.example: For 'crait', learner writes 'xqzt' — no phonetic relationship

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: REAL_WORD_SUB: explicit instruction 'write what you hear, not a real word'. Return to CVC nonsense words only.

atomic_skills.title: Complete Left-to-Right Grapheme Sequence
atomic_skills.description: Write every sound in a spoken word, in the correct left-to-right order — no sounds missing. The learner must account for every phoneme from the first sound to the last, with nothing skipped and nothing out of order.

error_signatures.description: The same position in words is omitted repeatedly
error_signatures.example: Learner consistently omits the final consonant across multiple words

error_signatures.description: Phonemes swapped in the encoded output
error_signatures.example: For 'was', learner types 'saw'

error_signatures.description: Extra phoneme represented in the encoding
error_signatures.example: For 'cat', learner types 'catt'

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: OMISSION_PATTERN: identify the position; drill targeting that slot. TRANSPOSITION: left-to-right sweep cue before encoding.

atomic_skills.title: Phonetic Self-Correction of Implausible Encodings
atomic_skills.description: When a spelling attempt is wrong, go back and fix it using sound reasoning — not guessing. The learner notices that their spelling doesn't match the sounds in the word and makes a targeted correction, not a random one.

error_signatures.description: The change shows no phonetic improvement — revision is random
error_signatures.example: Learner changes 'xqzt' to 'xqzp' — neither has phonetic logic

error_signatures.description: Learner never revises even when output is implausible
error_signatures.example: Learner submits 'xqzt' for 'cat' without any attempt to self-check

error_signatures.description: Revision is more complex but less plausible than the original
error_signatures.example: Learner changes a plausible 'kat' to an implausible 'cqat'

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: RANDOM_REVISION: teach the check strategy 'say it slowly, tap each sound, match letters'. NO_SELF_CORRECTION: prompt 'Check: does every sound have a letter?'

levels.title: Decoding & Fluency Construction
levels.description: Read aloud smoothly, in phrases, at a natural pace. Grade 2–3, voice required. Unlocks after Hard Gate 1. Read at 60 or more words per minute, with a prosody (phrasing) score of 70% or above, and a self-correction rate of 50% or above — confirmed across 2 separate sessions by voice.

atomic_skills.title: Accurate Phonetic Word Decoding
atomic_skills.description: Read unfamiliar phonetic words aloud, producing each sound correctly. The learner sees a word they haven't memorised and reads it by applying their phonics knowledge — each sound in the right order, nothing skipped.

error_signatures.description: A phoneme replaced by a different phoneme
error_signatures.example: For 'pin', learner reads 'pan'

error_signatures.description: A phoneme absent from the spoken output
error_signatures.example: For 'step', learner reads 'sep'

error_signatures.description: Output phonemically unrelated to target — visual guessing detected
error_signatures.example: For 'drip', learner says 'drop' — visually similar but phonemically wrong

error_signatures.description: Response time exceeds 5 seconds
error_signatures.example: Learner stares at the word for 6 seconds before attempting

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: PHONEME_SUB: identify substitution pattern (onset/coda/vowel?) and drill that phonogram. WHOLE_WORD_GUESS: return to L3 encoding.

atomic_skills.title: Nonsense Word Oral Decoding
atomic_skills.description: Read made-up words aloud using the phonics code — not guessing from memory. Because the word has never been seen before, the only way to read it is to decode it sound by sound. Producing a real word instead is an automatic fail.

error_signatures.description: Reads a real word instead of decoding the nonsense word
error_signatures.example: For 'blof', learner reads 'blow'

error_signatures.description: Phoneme accuracy below 70% — output not recognisably related to target
error_signatures.example: For 'spund', learner produces a string that shares no sounds with the target

error_signatures.description: Learner refuses to attempt the nonsense word
error_signatures.example: Learner says 'That's not a real word, I can't read it'

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: REAL_WORD_SUB: explicit instruction 'read what you see'. REFUSAL: explain the purpose 'we're practising the code, not the word'.

atomic_skills.title: Left-to-Right Text Tracking
atomic_skills.description: Read words in the correct printed order from left to right, without skipping or repeating lines. The learner tracks each line consistently — no jumping ahead, no going back to a previous line, no missing words.

error_signatures.description: Learner reads from the wrong line
error_signatures.example: Learner jumps from line 2 to line 4, skipping line 3

error_signatures.description: Learner reads an earlier word out of sequence
error_signatures.example: Learner re-reads a word from the beginning of the line mid-passage

error_signatures.description: Repeats a word without intending to self-correct
error_signatures.example: Learner reads 'the the cat sat' without self-correcting the repeated 'the'

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: LINE_SKIP: text with explicit line guides; reduce column width. BACKWARD_JUMP: return to single-sentence texts.

atomic_skills.title: Elimination of Letter-by-Letter Sounding
atomic_skills.description: Stop sounding out letter-by-letter — read words as whole units. The learner recognises the full word pattern at once rather than sounding each letter individually. This is the shift from decoding to automatic word recognition.

error_signatures.description: Explicit subvocalised sounding of individual letters detected before the word is produced
error_signatures.example: Learner says /k/... /a/... /t/... then 'cat'

error_signatures.description: First 1-2 letters sounded then word completed
error_signatures.example: Learner says /s/... /t/... then 'stop'

error_signatures.description: More than 3-second pause without any output
error_signatures.example: Learner stares at word for 4+ seconds in silence

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: LETTER_BY_LETTER: whole-word pattern flash drills; timed repeated reading. SILENT_STALL: return to single-word decoding.

atomic_skills.title: Phrased Reading with Prosody
atomic_skills.description: Read connected text in phrases of at least 2 words, pausing at punctuation rather than after every single word. Reading sounds natural and grouped — not robotic and word-by-word. Punctuation marks shape the phrasing.

error_signatures.description: Prosody score falls below 60%
error_signatures.example: Learner pauses randomly throughout sentences rather than at punctuation

error_signatures.description: Pause detected after every single word
error_signatures.example: Learner reads 'The... cat... sat... on... the... mat'

error_signatures.description: Fluent phrasing present but reading rate below 40 WPM
error_signatures.example: Learner groups words correctly but reads very slowly

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: LOW_PROSODY: echo reading — system models a phrase, learner echoes. WORD_BY_WORD: mark phrase boundaries before reading; teach punctuation cues.

atomic_skills.title: Self-Monitoring for Meaning During Reading
atomic_skills.description: Notice when a word doesn't make sense in context, and re-read to fix it. The learner catches their own errors by listening to whether the sentence makes sense — then goes back and reads the problem word correctly.

error_signatures.description: Zero self-corrections despite meaning violations occurring
error_signatures.example: Learner reads 'The horse sat on the house' without correcting 'horse' for 'mouse'

error_signatures.description: Re-reads correct segments unnecessarily
error_signatures.example: Learner re-reads correctly decoded words multiple times without error

error_signatures.description: Visually similar but semantically wrong word used and not corrected
error_signatures.example: Reads 'horse' for 'house' — visually similar, semantically wrong

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: NO_MONITOR: post-passage check 'Did everything make sense?'. DECODING_SUB: return to L4.A1 phoneme accuracy drills.

levels.title: Comprehension & Language Expansion
levels.description: Understand what you read and explain your thinking. Grade 3, voice + text. Unlocks after Level 4. Literal comprehension at 80% or above, inferential comprehension at 75% or above, and written response completeness at 80% or above — across 2 separate sessions.

atomic_skills.title: Literal Comprehension with Text Evidence
atomic_skills.description: Answer questions about facts stated directly in the text, and point to the words that support their answer. The learner finds the evidence in the passage itself — not from general knowledge or guessing.

error_signatures.description: Answer is factually correct but no text evidence used
error_signatures.example: Learner gives correct answer but uses only their own words with no reference to the text

error_signatures.description: Answer expressed in own words but the meaning has changed
error_signatures.example: Learner paraphrases a sentence but alters the meaning in the process

error_signatures.description: Factually wrong answer given
error_signatures.example: Learner states something that contradicts what the text says

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: NO_TEXT_REF: text-reference habit drill — system highlights the relevant sentence; learner must locate and reference it before answering.

atomic_skills.title: Inferential Comprehension with Connector and Evidence
atomic_skills.description: Draw conclusions that aren't directly stated — and explain the reasoning using words like 'because' or 'this shows that'. The learner reads between the lines and justifies their thinking with evidence from the text.

error_signatures.description: Conclusion not supported by evidence in the text
error_signatures.example: Learner draws a conclusion that contradicts or has no basis in the text

error_signatures.description: Conclusion stated without any linking language
error_signatures.example: Learner states conclusion but omits 'because', 'therefore', or similar connective

error_signatures.description: Restates a fact from the text without drawing any conclusion
error_signatures.example: Instead of inferring, learner just quotes a sentence from the passage

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: NO_CONNECTOR: model inference think-aloud 'This shows ___ because ___ in the text says ___.' Learner attempts with the scaffolded connector.

atomic_skills.title: Oral or Written Retell with Main Idea and Supporting Details
atomic_skills.description: Retell or summarise a passage including the main idea and at least 2 supporting details. The learner captures what the passage was mostly about, plus the key details that back it up — in a logical order.

error_signatures.description: Only details listed with no overarching main point
error_signatures.example: Learner lists three events but never states what the passage was about overall

error_signatures.description: n-gram similarity to source text exceeds 70% — output is a near-copy
error_signatures.example: Learner reproduces sentences verbatim from the passage

error_signatures.description: Disconnected list without logical connectors between ideas
error_signatures.example: Learner lists facts with no 'first', 'then', 'because', or other connectors

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: NO_STRUCTURE: graphic organiser — 3-box structure (Main idea / Detail 1 / Detail 2). Learner fills verbally or in text before writing. Scaffold removed when organiser-independent summaries reach 80%.

atomic_skills.title: Reasoning Connective Use — Linking Evidence to Conclusions
atomic_skills.description: Use connecting words (because, however, therefore, this means that) to link evidence to conclusions. The learner doesn't just state what they think — they use language that shows the logical connection between the evidence and the point they're making.

error_signatures.description: Conclusion stated with no linking language at all
error_signatures.example: Learner states 'The character was scared. He ran away.' — no connector

error_signatures.description: Connective present but linking the wrong ideas together
error_signatures.example: Learner uses 'because' but connects unrelated clauses incorrectly

error_signatures.description: Connective used but no text evidence provided to support it
error_signatures.example: Learner says 'He was scared because...' but provides no evidence from the text

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: CONNECTOR_ABSENT: sentence frame 'I know this because the text says ___.' CONNECTOR_MISUSED: explicit modelling of the logical relationship.

atomic_skills.title: Contextually Accurate Vocabulary Use
atomic_skills.description: Use newly taught vocabulary words correctly in their own sentences. The learner demonstrates that they understand what a word means by using it in a sentence where it makes sense — not just repeating it back.

error_signatures.description: Word used with semantic plausibility score below 0.4 — meaning is wrong in context
error_signatures.example: Learner uses 'enormous' to describe something very small

error_signatures.description: Learner provides a definition of the word but does not actually use it in a sentence
error_signatures.example: Learner says 'enormous means very big' instead of using it in a sentence

error_signatures.description: Learner uses a different word instead of the target vocabulary word
error_signatures.example: Asked to use 'enormous', learner uses 'big' instead

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: VOCAB_MISUSE: system presents 3 more example sentences. Learner attempts again. Second failure: demote from active vocabulary list; re-present in next session.

atomic_skills.title: Structured Written Response with Topic Sentence and Connectives
atomic_skills.description: Write a structured response with a clear topic sentence, supporting details, complete sentences, and connective language. The learner organises their writing so that the main point comes first, the evidence follows, and the language holds it all together.

error_signatures.description: Complete sentence rate below 60% in a 5-sentence response — fragments throughout
error_signatures.example: Learner writes 'Cat. Running fast. No stop.' instead of full sentences

error_signatures.description: n-gram similarity to source text above 70% AND no connector words — copied text with no structure
error_signatures.example: Learner reproduces large portions of the source text with no original organisation

error_signatures.description: Keyword overlap with source text below 1 term in more than 60% of answers
error_signatures.example: Written response makes no reference to anything in the passage

atomic_skills.recovery_strategy: ERR_FRAGMENTS: reduce to 1-sentence minimum. Oral rehearsal — learner speaks the sentence before writing. Sentence frames active until complete sentence rate reaches 85%.
